_doc: PRE-REGISTERED candidate list + evaluation contract for the MORNING-SESSION ENTRY GATE test (PROFIT-P3-MORNING-GATE-PREREG). Frozen BEFORE any candidate is run (exploratory != confirmatory -- no re-picks after seeing results; FAIL is publishable). REGISTRATION ONLY: this file specifies the exact hypothesis, gate candidates, population, window, battery, and kill bar. The run is dispatched separately once the OPRA option-bar cache is free (another crew is using it at freeze time -- see scheduling_note). No test was executed to produce this file.
runner: NOT YET BUILT -- proposed path backtest/tools/morning_gate_study.py. This file is the exact contract that runner must satisfy: same population/window/battery/pass-bar as specified here, no substitutions without a new frozen version.
scheduling_note: The OPRA option-bar cache (backtest/data/options/, 8,669 contract CSVs) is in concurrent use by another crew (FDR-16 real-fills confirmation + P5 top-cell confirm) at freeze time. This study's evaluation window needs the SAME cache for its option-premium math (TP1 distance, ribbon_ride entry premiums) -- queued to run sequentially after that crew finishes, per the project's own 'one grind at a time on the OPRA cache' discipline (queue.md PROFIT-P2 carries the identical dependency note).
hypothesis: 0DTE ribbon_ride entries taken before some morning cutoff have structurally worse expectancy than entries taken after it, over the FULL trading history (not just the 9-day sample that generated the hypothesis) -- driven by lower morning liquidity / wider spreads / whipsaw price action reading as premium-stop noise (the SAME noise-floor mechanism already documented for sub-$0.20 entries, journal memory 2026-07-08).

hypothesis_provenance.generated_by: analysis/deep-research/2026-07-11-ledger-forensics.md section 2: every MORNING-bucket (entry <11:00 ET) engine episode in the 2026-06-26..2026-07-09 window premium-stopped -- n=34/34, 0% win rate, -$1,463.99. Fully contained inside the premium-stop mechanism (not incremental dollars), but the sharpest single predictor found in that report.
hypothesis_provenance.secondary_source: markdown/research/EXTERNAL-0DTE-MECHANISMS-2026-07-11.md mechanism #2 (time-of-day structure): practitioner-converged (thinner than academic) evidence for an 11:00 ET auction / low-activity midday chop window; explicitly flagged there as the cheapest test in the whole external sweep ('costs nothing but a pandas.groupby on trades you already have').
hypothesis_provenance.exclusion_rationale: This 9-day window generated the hypothesis (34/34 morning losers). Testing the gate's benefit ON the window that produced it would be circular -- the pre-registered evaluation below runs ONLY on history outside this window (no peeking).

primary.rationale: The hypothesis-source cohort (34/34 morning losers) is dominated by these two setups in the ledger-forensics report (BULLISH_RECLAIM n=65 / BEARISH_REJECTION n=24 of 109 engine episodes system-wide). This is the population the gate is scoped to PASS/FAIL against.

explicit_exclusion.rationale: These setups are STRUCTURALLY morning-native by their own validated design -- vwap_continuation requires 'FIRST morning bar (<=10:30 ET) that continues in-trend' (params.json _j_vwap_cont_doc), j_vwap_reclaim_fb requires the break+reclaim sequence to resolve '<=10:30 ET', j_vix_dayside's entry window is literally '09:35-11:30 ET morning window' (params.json docs). A blanket engine-wide morning gate would silently neuter setups that were independently validated (real-fills, C1) to trade THAT exact window. C29 (exit/entry knobs never transfer across setups without independent verification) applies here to entry gates too -- this scoping decision is the P3 equivalent of that rule. These setups are NOT touched by any candidate below regardless of outcome.

secondary_disclosure_only.scope: all engine-attributed entries system-wide (every setup, every account), same window
secondary_disclosure_only.role: reported alongside the primary result for context ONLY -- not gated by its own pass bar. Mirrors the elite/super-cohort disclosure pattern used in analysis/recommendations/block-elite-bull-ssb-preregistration.json.

gate_mechanics.statement: Each candidate is an ENTRY-TIME FLOOR, mechanically identical in kind to the existing v15.3 09:35 ET entry-gate floor already live in the engine (params.json entry window doctrine) -- it simply moves that floor later for the in-scope setups. A signal whose bar timestamp (ET) falls inside [09:35, cutoff) produces SKIP instead of ENTER; the signal is not re-evaluated later (no queued/deferred entry) -- exactly how the existing 09:35 floor behaves today.
gate_mechanics.applies_to: signal bar ET timestamp, not fill timestamp (matches every other time-gate in this engine, e.g. no_trade_before/time_stop_et).

V1_GATE_BEFORE_11.label: block all in-scope entries with signal bar ET < 11:00:00
V1_GATE_BEFORE_11.rationale: Matches the EXACT ledger-forensics MORNING-bucket boundary that produced the 34/34 finding -- the most direct test of the hypothesis as stated.

V2_GATE_BEFORE_1030.label: block all in-scope entries with signal bar ET < 10:30:00
V2_GATE_BEFORE_1030.rationale: Narrower variant -- tests whether a tighter cutoff captures most of the benefit at lower participation cost (fewer entries blocked). Matches the external mechanism sweep's convergence on a ~60-minute opening-range structure (EXTERNAL-0DTE-MECHANISMS-2026-07-11.md #2, 'Option Alpha ORB explainer').

V3_GATE_FIRST_HOUR.label: block all in-scope entries within the first 60 minutes of the entry window's own open (09:35-10:35 ET), NOT a fixed wall-clock cutoff
V3_GATE_FIRST_HOUR.cutoff_definition: entry_window_open_et (09:35:00, the existing v15.3 floor) + 60 minutes
V3_GATE_FIRST_HOUR.rationale: Deliberately anchored to the SESSION'S entry-window open rather than a round wall-clock number -- distinct in kind from V2 even though the two cutoffs are only 5 minutes apart (10:30 vs 10:35). Disclosed: given the 5-minute gap, expect V2 and V3 to produce near-identical populations on most days; reported as two candidates anyway because the pre-registration was frozen before the run and the task named both explicitly.

opra_option_cache_coverage_at_freeze.verified_by: directory listing of backtest/data/options/*.csv at freeze time -- 8,669 contract files, earliest SPY250102*, latest SPY260708*

evaluation_window.exclusion_boundary_note: 2026-07-09 has no OPRA option-cache coverage at freeze time anyway (cache ends 2026-07-08), so the effective exclusion is bounded by the cache's own end date -- the task's stated exclusion window and the cache boundary agree, not a coincidence to resolve.

is_oos_split.convention_source: matches the established calendar-year OOS_BOUNDARY used across backtest/autoresearch/family_grind.py, fleet_gate_sweetspot.py, gate_frequency_frontier.py -- reused for consistency, not reinvented.

evaluation_window.signal_population_source: the SAME full-history ribbon_ride signal-generation path that originally produced the setup (family_grind.py / the mass-grind funnel per strategies.py's own provenance comment: 'ribbon_ride: the mass-grind funnel winner, 2026-06-25') -- the runner MUST reuse that generator, not a re-derived signal set, so this study's population is consistent with the setup's own validation history. If the exact generator call differs from what ships, the runner discloses the diff before reporting results (no silent population substitution).

1_expectancy.metric: per-trade dollar expectancy AND total pnl, gate-ON (candidate applied) vs gate-OFF (baseline, no morning gate) on the primary population/window.
1_expectancy.pass_condition: gate-ON per-trade expectancy > gate-OFF per-trade expectancy (STRICTLY greater -- a tie is not a pass), computed via lib.simulator_real.simulate_trade_real on the SAME signal population for both arms (only entry inclusion differs).

2_oos.metric: condition 1 evaluated separately on the IS (2025) and OOS (2026, post-exclusion) slices.
2_oos.pass_condition: gate-ON beats gate-OFF in BOTH slices (matches the project's own WF/OOS discipline -- an IS-only win is not sufient, per this repo's C4/C29 disclosure norms).

3_random_entry_null.purpose: isolates whether the BLOCKED cohort's poor performance is specific to this setup's morning signal quality, or a generic property of ANY entry taken in that time window (C3/L58 exit-structure-artifact logic, applied to a gate instead of a new signal).
3_random_entry_null.method: autoresearch.null_baseline.random_entry_null, restricted to entry_gate=(09:35, cutoff_et) for the candidate under test, matched n_signals/n_call/n_put/strike_offset/premium_stop_pct to the REMOVED (blocked) cohort's own realized values, 10 deterministic seeds (module default).
3_random_entry_null.pass_condition: the blocked cohort's OWN realized per-trade expectancy is <= the random-entry null's per_trade_mean for that same window -- i.e. the setup's morning trades are not meaningfully BETTER than a coin-flip morning entry (if they were, blocking them would be throwing away signal, not noise).

4_opposite_null.purpose: negative control -- rules out 'blocking any N% of trades looks like an improvement by construction/variance' rather than a genuine morning-specific mechanism.
4_opposite_null.method: mirror-image gate: instead of blocking [09:35, cutoff_et), block a LAST-part-of-session window of comparable blocked-trade-COUNT (e.g. [X, 15:00) sized so the blocked n matches the candidate's blocked n +/-10%), same population/window, same battery stage 1 metric.
4_opposite_null.pass_condition: the mirror-image (late-session) gate does NOT produce a comparable or larger expectancy improvement than the morning candidate. If it does, the morning-specific story is not supported -- flag as a kill signal even if stage 1 nominally passed.

5_concentration.metric: drop-top-3 (t4_exit_matrix.py battery() convention: remove the 3 highest-pnl trades, recompute) applied independently to the KEPT (gate-ON survivors) and REMOVED (blocked) cohorts.
5_concentration.pass_condition: gate-ON's drop-top-3 expectancy still beats gate-OFF's drop-top-3 expectancy -- the improvement must not depend on 1-3 outlier trades in either direction.

6_bh_fdr.method: backtest/autoresearch/ribbon_rejection_wick_battery.py's bh_fdr() at FDR_ALPHA=0.10 (this repo's standing convention, reused not reinvented), applied across the 3 candidate_ids_in_multiplicity_correction.
6_bh_fdr.pass_condition: candidate's stage-1 p-value/effect survives BH-FDR correction at alpha=0.10 across the 3-way comparison -- guards against one of three candidates looking significant by chance.

kill_criteria.statement: ANY of the following kills the candidate outright, regardless of other stages:
kill_criteria.k1: stage 1 (expectancy) fails on the full net window.
kill_criteria.k2: stage 2 (OOS) fails on either the IS or OOS slice alone (a candidate that only helps in one calendar year is not shipped).
kill_criteria.k3: stage 4 (opposite_null) shows the late-session mirror gate produces a comparable-or-larger improvement -- the effect is not morning-specific.
kill_criteria.k4: stage 6 (BH-FDR) rejects the candidate at alpha=0.10 after multiplicity correction.
kill_criteria.k5_scope_violation: the runner's population accidentally includes any explicitly-excluded setup (vwap_continuation / j_vwap_reclaim_fb / j_vix_dayside) -- a structural bug, not a numeric outcome; must be fixed and re-verified before any candidate is reported, not silently absorbed into the result.

pass_bar.aggregation: AND of stages 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 -- no partial credit, matching this repo's standing pre-registration convention (structure-stop-preregistration.json pass_bar.aggregation).
pass_bar.min_n_disclosure: a candidate's kept AND removed cohort n must each be reported with the result; n<20 on either side is INSUFFICIENT_N (this project's own live-graduation floor, CLAUDE.md) and the candidate is reported as inconclusive, not passed or failed.

anchor_context_check.purpose: disclosure-only cross-check (not a pass/fail gate) -- verify no candidate would have blocked a source-of-truth J anchor trade, per the same discipline OP-16 already applies to strike/exit changes.

anchors_in_scope.note: the 3 winners are dated within the net evaluation window (2025-01-02..2026-06-25) and are pre-fleet (journal/trades.csv, no broker-ledger coverage per ledger-forensics.md section 1) -- their exact intraday ENTRY TIME must be pulled from journal/YYYY-MM-DD.md for this check, not assumed from the summary table.

anchor_context_check.reporting_requirement: if any candidate's cutoff would have blocked a winner's actual entry time, state it explicitly and flag the candidate MISCALIBRATED regardless of aggregate battery result (mirrors EXTERNAL-0DTE-MECHANISMS-2026-07-11.md mechanism #1's identical anchor-check instruction for the expected-move gate).

no_repick_clause: Once this file is frozen, no cutoff time, population scope, window, or battery definition may be edited in light of results. A FAIL (or an INSUFFICIENT_N on all 3 candidates) is a publishable, informative outcome, not a reason to adjust the pre-registration and re-run.
